steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease baking sheets.

To make the cookie dough: Combine brown sugar and oil in a bowl. Mix in pumpkin and eggs, beating well. Add flour, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, salt, baking powder, baking soda, and vanilla together into a separate bowl. Fold dry ingredients into wet ingredients and mix to combine.
Drop dough by heaping teaspoons onto the prepared baking sheets.

Bake in the preheated oven until cookies spring back when lightly touched, 10 to 12 minutes . Cool on baking sheets briefly before transferring to wire racks to cool completely while you make the filling.

To make the whoopie pie filling: Beat egg white in a bowl and mix in milk, vanilla, then 1 cup confectioners' sugar. Mix well then beat in shortening and remaining 1 cup confectioners' sugar. Beat until light and fluffy.
Assemble once cookies are cool. Make sandwiches from two cookies filled with whoopie pie filling.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Whoopie Pies
raw_recipe.description: Pumpkin whoopie pies with a simple, sweet filling make a perfect treat everyone is sure to love. These are a perfect addition to the holiday table.

video.description: In this video, you'll see how to make Pumpkin Whoopie Pies. We first bake a batch of pumpkin-flavored cookies. They are great on their own, but we take them a step further and sandwich two cookies with creamy filling.
video.name: How to Make Pumpkin Whoopie Pies

review.reviewBody: These are absolutely DELICIOUS. I made the batter as directed. The first batch of cookies flattened too much, but after the batter had sat for about 10 minutes, it thickened nicely and the cookies were perfect. I used a 2 tbsp. mini ice cream scoop so they'd be the same size, and I had no problems with them keeping a funky shape while baking. They smoothed out perfectly. I used a different filling: 1 large tub Cool Whip, 8 oz cream cheese, 2/3 cup sugar and 2 tsp. vanilla, whipped together. It was light, not too rich. The flavor of the pies was much better after they rested overnight. MAKE THIS RECIPE. You won't be disappointed.

these bake up so beautifully. I used 3 tsp of pumpkin pie spice in place of the individual spices. for the filling, I beat the egg white to stiff peaks. The filling was a beautiful consistency, much like buttercream, very light and fluffly. I used my large size Pampered Chef cookie scoop to get uniform cookies. The amount of filling is just perfect for the cookies. I sprinkled some fall colored sprinkles on the edges to attach to the filling and they looked so pretty. thanks for this wonderful recipe. Will definitely make again.

I made these yesterday, and in one word...AMAZING!!! To give you a sense of how great these are, I made these for my daughter to take to work for a celebration. She took these this morning, it's now 9AM and she just texted me that they're 70% gone. She said people LOVE them and I should start selling them. I applied two small game changers however...

I followed the cake recipe exactly, but like other reviewers, I subbed in a cream cheese filling. It was 1/2 cup of butter beat for 3 minutes. Then I added 8 ounces of cream cheese and beat another 3 minutes. Then I added 1 tsp vanilla and beat in. Finally, 3 cups of powdered sugar, added in thirds and beat in. I used a one ounce cookie scoop for the batter and the filling and this recipe yielded 26 pies.

The other game changer...after everything was assembled and each wrapped in plastic wrap, I refrigerated them. OMG!!! The filling becomes CRAZY GOOD.

GREAT and Easy Recipe.
(My Variation)
Use Cake Flour for a Fluffier consistency.
I opted for a different whipped Cream Frosting instead.
8 oz of cream cheese
1 cup of Sugar
1 Teasp of Vanilla
1/8 teasp of Salt
(Mixed and smooth together)
(In a Separate bowl whip)
1-1/2 cups of cold Heavy Whipping Cream (Until stiff peaks appear)
Incorporate the Cream Cheese mixture to the Whipped Cream.

I made the whoopie pie batter as directed. Let the batter rest while the oven is heating (10-15 mins.)as it will thicken a bit and not spread. I did use a cream cheese icing to fill the whoopie pies. Piping the icing with a large decorating tip speeds up the filling of the pies. I used one 15 oz can of pumpkin puree minus a tablespoon to equal 1.5 cups. I wrapped each individual pie in cling wrap so we could "grab and go." We love them!

I followed the instructions near perfectly (except I added a whole 15 once can of pumpkin) and this made a great tasting moist cookie, but I did find one major problem--for me at least. The baking time as written (10 minutes) was far from accurate and left me with underdone and doughy cookies. I baked them on a nonstick whoopie pie pan and used a tablespoon sized cookie scoop. That size needed about 17 minutes at 350° and it still came out really moist. I needed wax paper to keep them from sticking to each other or the plate I stored them on. I highly recommend always baking a tiny sample amount first when trying a new recipe. This recipe as written made nearly 40 whoopie pies for me. Note: I DID NOT make the filling on this recipe, just the cookie. I bought a pre-made whipped frosting and that worked just fine.

Amazing! I followed the recipe exactly for the cookie/cake/pie part. I used a melon baller so that I had mini versions. For the filling I did the same as the review below... 1 big tub cool whip, 8oz cream cheese 2/3c powdered sugar and 2 tsp vanilla! AMAZING!!!

These are magical! I did make a few revisions because I was making it for my son's 3rd grade class. I pretty much halved all the spices, but if I were to have just made it for my family, I definitely would've kept the original amount. I added a bit of allspice, more pumpkin, more brown sugar (I wanted a denser "cookie"), and filled them with a cream cheese frosting. If you really care about consistency in shape and size, I scooped the batter into a whoopie pie/muffin top pan with a small cookie scoop and made sure to spread it out to the edges. They came out perfectly and everyone loved them.

The cakes were delicious, I did decide to pipe them out because the batter spread unevenly. I used my own Whoopie Cake recipe for the filling, 1/2 c. butter, 1/2 c. Crisco, 1/2 c. Marshmallow creme, 1 c. powdered sugar. Also tried adding some cream cheese to the filling, which was pretty tasty. I will definitely be making these again.

Perfect Pumpkin Whoopie Pies!!!! I had to use Butter instead of vegetable oil because I had none on hand. I also had to use one cup of white sugar and one cup of brown sugar instead of two cups of brown sugar. TIP: I suggest using a SMALL ice cream scoop or cookie dough scoop when scooping the batter on a baking sheet, because when I used a med to large scooper the whoopie pies were spread out, really big, and close together. However, they still tasted amazing!!!

I doubled the recipe for a bake sale fundraising for on of our sons, it was easy and so yummy! Used a 1" melon ball/cookie dough scoop for more precision sized/shaped cookies and they came out perfectly. 
I balled the dough onto parchment paper for easy lift and cooked for 11.5 min per baking sheet full. The frosting is perfect consistency and also VERY easy to make. Whipped my whites to soft peaks before adding other ingredients. Delish!

Even if you don't like pumpkin pie, this is one of those desserts that are universally loved. They don't have that pumpkin pie pumpkiny taste. These just taste like Fall! So moist, not to sweet, amazing with a cup of coffee! All five of us with different tastebuds wanted more. Tip: I would make 25% more filling next time. We ran out and had 2 cakes with no filling. :(

I used this recipe for the first time and made it as directed. The dough was way too wet and difficult to work with. The cookies fall apart when you try to eat them. I’m guessing it’s the one cup of oil. I let the batter sit to thicken before baking as suggested in reviews but it did not help. They taste delicious but are messy and “wet”. I baked them for at least the maximum time. I won’t be using this recipe again.
These were lovely! So easy to make and everyone loved them! I will definitely make these again 😀

I loved these whoopie pies! I made half the recipe amount for the cookies, and opted to use a cream cheese filling. (Not a fan of the raw egg white and shortening in the recipe's filling.) I agree with the other reviewers that state to let the cookie batter rest for a few minutes before scooping onto the baking sheets. This will allow the batter to thicken slightly and make for easier scooping, and nicer looking cookies. I loved how soft the cookies came out. Perfectly spiced, not too sweet--and with a cream cheese filling, they were TDF. I will say not to stack these when storing them. They will stick horribly to each other and tear apart. They might do better when chilled, but at room temp they stuck somethin' fierce. Overall though, I really enjoyed these. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

Outstanding recipe... when I prepared the batter, I added the vanilla to the "wet" ingredients instead of after the "dry" ingredients had been added. It becomes a rather thick batter and wasn't sure the vanilla would blend in evenly.

Made the cookies exactly as directed but used another reviewer’s suggestion with a cream cheese filling. Gave them to my grandchildren for Halloween and they loved them! The “cookie” part was dense with flavor yet still moist and cake-like. They looked small but they were very rich and delicious! Making them again for a bake sale! This time I may change up the filling again to a cream cheese/ whipped topping combination!

I made the batter 5 days ago and never got around to baking them. Today, I took care of that and they baked up wonderfully. I don't care for shortening in my frostings so I substitute butter as another person recommended.
These little pies are so much work, but they are worth it! I used butter instead of shortening and it turned out great.
Too much filling. Could have made little over half the recipe.
